senses.gloss: simile, illustration (cmp. מָשָׁל ל־, משל למה הדבר דומה). Cant. R., introd. עד … היתה ד׳ up to Solomon’s days the method of argument by illustration was unknown (in Hebrew literature).

units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3:1:2">Y. Hor. III, beg. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>די׳ דידכו דמי וכ׳</he> (prob. to be read <he>דמיא</he>) your appearance resembles that of your Maker.

Eduy. V, 6; Ber. 19ᵃ ד׳ השקוה it was for show that they made her drink, i.e. they merely pretended to give her the real ‘bitter waters’; [oth. opin. they performed the act on one who was, like themselves, a descendant of gentiles; Y. M. Kat. III, 81ᵈ דִּכְמָהּ השקוה, (a popular adaptation of our w.; v. דִּכְמָא), expl. דִּכְוָותָהּ something like it]. Midr. Sam. ch. XX (expl. תפקד לשלום, I Sam. XVII, 18) ד׳ דידהין how they look.

<cite ref="Chagigah 16a:2">Ḥag. 16ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>ד̇ג̇ול מ̇רבבה</he>, <cite ref="Song of Songs 5:10">Cant. V, 10</cite>) <he>ד̇וג̇מ̇א הוא ברבבה שלו</he> He is exemplified by His myriad (of angels), i.e. the Divine nature is recognized indirectly from the nature of His ministering messengers, v.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:9">Cant. R. to V, 9</cite>.—
<cite ref="Ketubot 28b:13">Keth. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>קחו לכם ד׳ וכ׳</he> take a warning example &c.
<cite ref="Taanit 23a:2">Taan. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>ד׳ לדורות</he> a sample (of great fertility) as a lesson for future generations.
<cite ref="Shabbat 30b">Sabb. 30ᵇ I</cite> will show thee <he>דּוּגְמָתָן וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>דּוּגְמָתוֹ</he>) the like thereof in this world.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 11b">Ib. 11ᵇ</cite> the dyer must not go out on the Sabbath <he>בדו׳ שבצוארו</he> (Ar. <he>בדי׳ שבאזנו</he>; Tosef. ib. I, 8 <he>בדו׳ שבאזנו</he>) with the sample of colors around his neck, v. <cite ref="A00940"><he>אוֹת</he> II</cite>.—

<cite ref="Job 36:7">Job XXXVI, 7</cite> <cite ref="P00622"><he>עיניו</he></cite>) <he>ד׳ דידהו</he> that which is like his own doing, i.e. some realization of his ideal, v. <cite ref="P00602"><he>עֵינָא</he></cite>; Midr. Sam. ch. XXVIII <he>דוגמה דידהון</he>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> <he>דוגמת דידיה</he> (corr. acc.), v. <cite ref="D00191">next w.</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>דּוּגְמוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 119b:10">B. Kam. 119ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="A00939"><he>אוֹת</he></cite> II (Var. Ms. <he>דּוּגְמָאוֹת</he>). [Our w., owing to its phonetic resemblance to <cite ref="D00781"><he>דִּכְמָא</he></cite>, is inflected as though it were a native, whence the forms: <cite ref="D00190"><he>דּוּגְמָה</he></cite>, <he>דּוּגְמת</he>, <he>דוּגְמָת־</he>, <he>דּוּגְמוֹת</he>, and even a Var. to <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 1:8">Tosef. Sabb. I, 8</cite> <he>דִּגְמוֹ</he>, as though fr. <cite ref="D00115"><he>דֶּגֶם</he></cite>.]
